findings.evidence: Re-read current file: stopRecording()'s null-path branch is now `if (path == null) { if (state.recordingPhase != RecordingPhase.recorded) { emit(state.copyWith(recordingPhase: RecordingPhase.idle)); } return; }`. This guards the idle transition on the phase not already being `recorded`, so a failed re-record after a prior successful recording no longer discards the `recorded` phase, while a genuinely fresh/never-recorded state (phase != recorded) still falls back to idle as before. Confirmed by the new regression test 'a failed re-record (stop() returns null after an earlier successful recording) preserves the recorded phase instead of regressing to idle' in test/unit/features/exam_attempt/read_aloud_cubit_test.dart:91-108, which asserts only a single `recorded` emission and no second emission on the subsequent null stop().

findings.evidence: Carried forward from phase 6's quality report (QUAL-601, still OPEN, unchanged by this diff): ReadAloudState.copyWith still computes `uploadStatus: uploadStatus ?? this.uploadStatus`. The cubit's watchRow listener calls `copyWith(uploadStatus: row == null ? null : ...)` intending to clear uploadStatus to null once the row disappears, but the null-coalescing operator makes an explicit null indistinguishable from an omitted argument, so the clearing branch can never execute.
findings.why_it_matters: Same latent footgun noted in phase 6: today the only row-to-null transition happens after a row reaches ready and gets deleted, so the stale non-null value is currently harmless, but a future flow reusing the same Cubit instance across a cleared row would silently keep showing a stale uploadStatus.
